# Consultation Contracts Checklist: Doctor Consultation Lifecycle

**Purpose**: Deep PR-review checklist for requirements quality in lifecycle API, upstream contracts, non-disclosure, transaction hand-off, and dependency boundaries.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## API Contract Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are request shapes and response fields specified for each lifecycle action, including whether the actions intentionally have no body? [Completeness, Contract §§Call Patient–Complete Consultation]
- [ ] CHK002 Are identifier format, path hierarchy, and hospital/branch cross-scope validation requirements explicitly documented? [Clarity, Contract introduction; Spec §FR-007–008]
- [ ] CHK003 Are malformed identifiers, absent records, out-of-scope records, invalid state, concurrent mutation, and unavailable recovery-boundary outcomes specified without ambiguity? [Completeness, Contract §§Call Patient–Complete Consultation]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the global error shape, codes, and messages required to remain non-disclosing across every protected lifecycle route? [Consistency, Contract §Error and Idempotency Semantics; Spec §FR-007–008]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the chosen non-idempotent repeat semantics for completed transitions consistent with the concurrency and recovery requirements? [Consistency, Contract §Error and Idempotency Semantics; Spec §FR-001–004, SC-002]

## Trusted Identity and Authority Boundaries

- [ ] CHK006 Are the trusted identity inputs, role assertions, branch/hospital scope, and doctor-assignment assertion defined as a minimal intentional contract? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007–008, FR-012; Data Model §External Contract Relationships]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the test-only trusted context requirement explicit about construction, isolation, and the prohibition on production routing or configuration? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions; Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK008 Are call/start/complete role requirements consistent between specification, data-model transition table, and API contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002–004, FR-012; Data Model §Allowed State Transitions; Contract §§Call Patient–Complete Consultation]
- [ ] CHK009 Are actor, role, hospital, branch, and scope excluded from all normal request inputs and protected from inference through error distinctions? [Security, Spec §FR-008; Contract §Error and Idempotency Semantics]

## Upstream and Recovery Contracts

- [ ] CHK010 Are check-in source-validation requirements specific about the queue-entry identity, eligibility state, hospital/branch/doctor match, and single-consultation guarantee? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, FR-013; Data Model §External Contract Relationships]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the queue-recalculation hand-off contract specified with an event identity, scope, idempotency behavior, acknowledgement, and the meaning of delivery status? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, FR-011; Data Model §Queue Recalculation Outbox]
- [ ] CHK012 Are retry cadence, ownership, duplicate delivery, recovery visibility, and terminal failure requirements documented for a durable queue hand-off? [Gap, Data Model §Queue Recalculation Outbox; Plan §Post-design]
- [ ] CHK013 Are audit-record contract fields and PII exclusions aligned with the trusted identity and transaction-boundary requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, FR-011; Data Model §Consultation Transition Audit]
- [ ] CHK014 Is branch-timezone availability and invalid-timezone handling specified as an upstream dependency without changing persisted instant semantics? [Gap, Spec §FR-005; Data Model §External Contract Relationships]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the preconditions that must be integrated before a consultation migration or endpoint is enabled clearly documented and traceable to the upstream owners? [Completeness, Plan §Integration prerequisite, §Structure Decision]

## Acceptance and Measurability

- [ ] CHK016 Are contract acceptance criteria defined for source-queue conflicts, wrong assigned doctor, cross-branch access, audit failure, queue hand-off failure, and retry duplication? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories, FR-006–013, SC-004–005]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the timing and failure-recovery success criteria measurable with fixture boundaries, concurrency counts, and an observable pass/fail outcome? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–005; Plan §Performance Goals]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
